track.status: built, ungated — 5,495 lines in 21 files. C2 cubic spline through a tridiagonal solve (not Catmull-Rom: a C1 interpolant puts a curvature jump at every knot and curvature is what a rider feels), rotation-minimising roll gauge, the spline IS the heartline 1.1 m above the rails. Ten primitive ops are the only switch in the module and it switches on the instruction set; 19 elements are DATA on top of them, with op arguments as expressions parsed by a hand-written parser rather than Function(), because packs load from URLs. Physics is a fixed-delta-s energy march. selftest.mjs: 95 checks, now wired into pnpm test:game.

demo-park.status: built, ungated — 1,610 lines; draws nothing itself, everything through terrain/paths/scenery/environment. 1,295 entities + 14,000 ambient instances, path graph 1,511 nodes / 4,022 edges / 17 junctions in ONE component, save 673.5 KB.

openIssues: STILL OPEN (track, its own #1): at 340 m a timber member is 0.26 m of real width against roughly 0.5 m per pixel, so 556 columns and their bracing sub-pixel-alias into a dark smear at the `overview` camera. Bracing alternate bays halved the member count and it is still visible. Needs a distance LOD that swaps the lattice for a coarser silhouette; the preset offers no MSAA. Confirmed by the integrator on `.game-render/track-verify/1200-overview.png` — the three layouts read as coaster shapes, the structure reads as speckle.

STILL OPEN (track): supports are vertical only, so any stretch rolled past 78 degrees gets none — a vertical column would meet the underside edge-on. On the three demo layouts this hits the corkscrew and the top of the loop, which are correctly unsupported in reality too, so nothing floats; a heavily overbanked layout would show gaps.

STILL OPEN (track): a layout is tuned for its train and nothing warns you. The ops shape themselves from a running-speed estimate that reads the train's drag area and rolling resistance, so a car 5 cm narrower builds a different track — two of three layouts closed 5 m worse under a hand-written train spec. A build tool that lets a player swap the train on an existing layout needs a rebuild-and-recheck API that does not exist.

`nextEntityId` kept a process-global `let idCounter` folded in with the world's own `__ids` by a `Math.max`, so the SECOND world built in a process carried on from where the first stopped — the same seed minted `path-1…` once and `path-4…` the next time (measured). Found by the demo-park builder, which builds its park twice to prove it reproduces. Fixed in core: the sequence lives in the world and nowhere else, and `test-game-save-roundtrip` now builds two worlds and compares, which was verified to FAIL with the counter put back.

STILL OPEN, measured on the finished park: a treeline CANNOT hide the world's edge. True horizon at screen row 153, the sky-to-land step at rows 228-240, the park boundary at row 268, and a 20 m tree on it tops out at 245 — below the thing it was meant to cover. Occluding the apron's rim from a 99 m camera needs about 65 m of planting. It is geometry (more apron, or a distance fade into the sky colour), not planting, and it stays terrain's.

STILL OPEN, measured: every tree in the `overview` frame is a LOD 2 imposter and the mid-ground reads as a palm grove — `linden:l2v0` x179, `spruce:l2v0` x351, `oak:l2v0` x288, and no LOD 0 tree mesh has an instance at that camera. At 42 m the same trees are convincing oaks with bark and branching. The break is at the pack's `lod[0] x 0.85 = 34 m`. It is scenery's `gen-foliage.ts` to fix; the demo park is where it shows.
Draw calls: 145 at `overview`, peak 237 at `ground` — 19.8 % of the 1,200 whole-game budget with six modules unbuilt, and roughly 127 of the 237 are shadow-map passes.

The sky, the fog and the exposure were all wrong in the same direction and are measured now. Three causes, each verified against a frame: (1) `scene.fogColor` was written as a LINEAR radiance, and Babylon runs `Color3.toLinearSpaceToRef` over it for every PBR material (`BindFogParameters`, `linearSpace` set), so the shader saw 0.034 where 0.295 was written — distant terrain got DARKER with distance instead of paler (sRGB 58/80/42 unfogged against 46/58/44 at 700 m). (2) The DOME painted `SkyState.ground` below the horizon, which is a term the IBL needs and the backdrop must not have: at the overview camera the terrain's far edge sits ~75 px under the true horizon and those 75 px were a dark olive band, sRGB 24/26/18 against the 75 the horizon ring rendered. That band is what several rounds of screenshots read as 'black above the horizon'. It is haze now — the azimuth's own horizon colour carried straight down, which is also the colour the fog takes the terrain to, so the edge dissolves instead of stepping. (3) The clear-day fog density was 0.0008, which with EXP2 plus Babylon's `toLinearSpace(fog)` put half the contrast of a surface 660 m away into the haze: a visibility of ~1.5 km on a day the model calls clear. 0.00035 now.

Auto exposure was a stop under and is 1.85x: EXPOSURE_KEY 0.42 -> 0.78, MIN 0.55 -> 1.0, MAX 2.2 -> 3.6. Those numbers were set against a frame in which the dome rendered black and the fog was four times too dark, so the scene they were metered against was not this scene. Measured at the old values: exposure settled at 1.054 and sunlit grass came out at 0.069 scene-linear, sRGB 80, where a photograph puts it near 120. Pinning exposure by hand and looking: 2.6 washes the grass towards yellow, 2.0 reads as a clear day.

The sky's shoulder ran per channel and therefore desaturated everything it touched — the horizon measured R:G:B 0.80 : 0.94 : 1.00 off the model and rendered grey. It runs on luminance now and scales all three channels by one factor. Measured on the model at noon, blue:red went 1.54 -> 2.81 at dy 0.3 and 2.05 -> 3.70 at dy 0.6, with the levels unchanged.

STILL OPEN, measured: the sky's horizon:zenith luminance ratio is about 4.5:1 where a real clear sky is nearer 2:1. That is Preetham's own horizon overshoot (it integrates an infinite air path with no ground and no aerosol scale-height cutoff), not the tone curve — lowering SKY_WHITE to fix it caps the sun's halo at 1.16x the horizon and flattens every sunset. The two candidate remedies are attenuating the near-horizon in-scattering in the model, or a separate curve for the solar lobe. Not attempted; SKY_GAIN stays 0.09.

STILL OPEN: at the overview camera the terrain's far edge is now a hard silhouette against the sky, because the fog that used to hide it was fog. The world simply ends about a kilometre out. That is the terrain module's geometry (world size, or a distant skirt), not the environment module's haze.

The camera fallback presets were wrong twice and are fixed twice: `overview` looked 37 degrees down against a 25.8-degree half-FOV, so the horizon was 11.3 degrees OUT of frame and no screenshot of that preset could contain sky; the correction to 23.5 degrees left 36 px of it, so every 'sky' screenshot after that was really a screenshot of the haze band. It is 15.5 degrees now, horizon at 154 px of 720.

20 of 24 modules are scaffolds: paths, pools, track, buildings, scenery, shops, rides, flumes, trains, guests, staff, management, overlays, tools, camera, scenarios, persistence, audio, effects, demo-park. The demo park renders an empty green hill: 47-74 draw calls, 31k-140k triangles.
